title: Security review: SSO / SCIM / RBAC for Redwood Private
summary: Redwood and Orion reviewed SSO (SAML) and SCIM provisioning flows for Redwood Private, walked through RBAC/least-privilege options, audit logging, data residency controls, and encryption/KMS integration. Action items: share SSO technical runbook, provide example SAML metadata + SCIM mapping, and propose RBAC role templates for least privilege.
next_steps: Alex: Send SSO runbook and sample SAML metadata (by 2025-07-24)
Priya: Share RBAC role templates and minimal permission set (by 2025-07-25)
Daniel: Provide list of test accounts and preferred IdP (by 2025-07-23)
Schedule follow-up checkpoint after IdP config (1 week)
action_items: Alex Chen - Send SSO/SCIM configuration guide + sample metadata - due 2025-07-24
Priya Patel - Draft RBAC role templates and least-privilege checklist - due 2025-07-25
Daniel Kim - Share Orion IdP SAML metadata and SCIM base URL - due 2025-07-23
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE. We also have Priya from our security engineering team.
[00:08] Maya Reyes: Hi Alex, hi Priya, thanks. I'm Maya, CISO at Orion. Daniel and Sara are here as well.
[00:14] Daniel Kim: Hey.
[00:15] Sara O'Neill: Hi all.
[00:18] Alex Chen: Quick agenda: SSO/SAML flow, SCIM provisioning, RBAC model, audit logs, encryption/KMS and data residency items. We'll leave time for Q&A. Sound good?
[00:27] Maya Reyes: Yep, sounds good. We're particularly interested in least-privilege RBAC and how provisioning works with our Okta setup.
[00:33] Priya Patel: Great. I'll start with SSO overview and how our Private deployment integrates with customer IdPs.
[00:40] Priya Patel: So for Redwood Private we support SAML 2.0 SP-initiated and IdP-initiated. You can host the control plane in your VPC or use our customer-managed control plane. SAML metadata exchange is standard — we provide the SP metadata, certs, and ACS URLs. It supports assertion consumer service binding post. There might be slight differences depending on Okta versions, but generally it's straightforward.
[01:12] Daniel Kim: When you say customer-managed control plane, is that running in our VPC?
[01:17] Priya Patel: Right, either our managed control plane deployed into your VPC (we ship a CloudFormation/Terraform module) or an on-prem package. In the VPC case the SSO handshake happens over internal endpoints; there's no public metadata leaked. For SCIM the provisioning endpoint is behind the private network.
[01:34] Maya Reyes: Ok. Our SecOps needs to know what attributes you need in the SAML assertion — name id, email, groups? Also we use Okta groups for role mapping.
[01:45] Alex Chen: Good question. We typically require nameidentifier/email and recommend groups for RBAC mapping. Priya, should we show the SCIM mapping example?
[01:52] Priya Patel: Yeah, quick example: we accept standard SCIM 2.0 attributes: userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type="work"].value, and groups. For provisioning we support create/update/delete and delta sync. We also have configurable attribute mappings so you can map your Okta group names to Redwood roles.
[02:16] Sara O'Neill: Is group membership synced automatically? We have nested groups in Okta.
[02:21] Priya Patel: Nested groups can be flattened at the IdP side or we can handle basic nested group traversal; depends on your provisioning setup. We'll show a sample mapping that flattens prefix.
[02:33] Daniel Kim: On the RBAC side, we want least privilege. What are the default roles and can we create custom roles?
[02:40] Priya Patel: We provide system roles: Owner, Admin, Developer, Viewer. Owners have full cluster/control plane access, Admins manage configs and users, Developers can create routes and see logs for their projects, Viewers read-only. You can define custom roles with a fine-grained permission set — e.g., allow create_endpoint but not manage_keys.
[02:58] Maya Reyes: Can RBAC be scoped to specific models/routes/environments? We want to give product teams deploy rights only to staging.
[03:06] Priya Patel: Yes, role scoping is hierarchical: org -> project -> route -> model. You can bind roles at the project level so someone can deploy only to a project/staging environment. We support role bindings via groups (SCIM group -> role).
[03:19] Alex Chen: Also we recommend least-privilege templates; Priya will share the templates after this call.
[03:25] Priya Patel: I'll add that. Also auditing: every auth event, provisioning change, role binding change is logged to the audit log with actor and request context. Logs can be shipped to your SIEM (S3, CloudWatch, Splunk, or syslog) and we support HMAC-signed delivery if you need integrity proofs.
[03:47] Maya Reyes: What's retention on the audit logs? We have retention requirements for 7 years for certain events.
[03:54] Priya Patel: Default retention in the platform is 90 days, but for Dedicated/Private we support configurable retention — you can set long-term retention to your S3 bucket or archive with lifecycle rules. For compliance workloads we often recommend exporting critical audit events to your retention store.
[04:12] Daniel Kim: Let's talk encryption and KMS. Can we bring our own KMS?
[04:17] Priya Patel: Yes, for Private you can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or an HSM via PKCS#11). We support envelope encryption: customer-managed CMK encrypts the data keys that encrypt model artifacts and logs. Access to keys is controlled via IAM roles we deploy in your account.
[04:36] Maya Reyes: Is there a key rotation process, and how are keys used for transit vs at-rest?
[04:42] Priya Patel: Keys are for at-rest encryption primarily; for transit we use TLS with mutual TLS options for inter-service comms inside VPC. Key rotation: you can schedule CMK rotation in your KMS; we recommend rotating data keys frequently. We also provide tooling to re-encrypt artifacts if you rotate a master key.
[04:58] Sara O'Neill: A quick question: if we provision users via SCIM and then a user leaves, what's the deprovision flow timeline?
[05:03] Priya Patel: Deprovisioning is near real-time if Okta pushes changes; otherwise we poll on a cadence (configurable, default 5 minutes). We can also disable sessions immediately when SCIM marks user inactive — that requires session sync which we support via a webhook.
[05:19] Maya Reyes: About sessions, do you have short-lived tokens, and can we set session lifetimes?
[05:24] Priya Patel: Yes, tokens are short-lived: access tokens default to 1 hour, refresh tokens 30 days, but in Private you can configure stricter policies, enforce IP/RBAC policies, and require MFA at the IdP.
[05:37] Daniel Kim: Regarding audit integrity, you mentioned HMAC-signed delivery. Do you support immutable append-only logs or merkle trees for tamper-evidence?
[05:47] Priya Patel: We don't currently provide merkle-tree-based logs out of the box, but we do support write-once append-only S3 with object lock (governance/compliance mode) and we sign each batch of logs with a customer-shared HMAC key. For higher assurance we can integrate with your ledger service; that's a custom engagement.
[06:08] Alex Chen: Maya, you had mentioned SOC 2 and ISO concerns — any specific controls you want to walk through?
[06:15] Maya Reyes: SOC 2 controls around logical access, change management, and logging. Also need to confirm encryption at rest keys are customer-controlled for regulated workloads.
[06:24] Priya Patel: For SOC 2 we map controls to our internal policies — we can share the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA. For encryption, as I said, in Private you can BYOK with KMS. For change management we maintain audit trails of deployments and config changes, and we can provide evidence of approvals if you use our integrations with ticketing systems.
[06:42] Sara O'Neill: Do you support SCIM group attribute sync that maps to multiple roles? We sometimes assign multiple roles via groups.
[06:49] Priya Patel: Yes, group-to-role mapping can be one-to-many. We'll share mapping examples: e.g., group "devs-staging" -> role deploy_staging plus role read_logs.
[06:59] Daniel Kim: On the technical side, what auth header do you expect on SCIM calls? Bearer token? Mutual TLS?
[07:06] Priya Patel: We support bearer token (OAuth2 client credentials) and mTLS for SCIM. For highest security we recommend mTLS + short-lived client certs managed by your PKI.
[07:17] Maya Reyes: Ok, we'd prefer mTLS. We'll need details for cert rotation and the CA chain.
[07:23] Priya Patel: We'll include the cert rotation recommendations in the runbook. Typically rotation is automated monthly for client certs, and the SCIM server validates CN and SAN.
[07:33] Alex Chen: Let's surface an example flow: Okta pushes new user via SCIM to Redwood Private SCIM endpoint (mTLS), Redwood creates user, maps groups to roles, logs event to audit log, and optionally exports to customer S3. Priya, correct?
[07:48] Priya Patel: Exactly. Also, we annotate the audit record with request-id, source IP, actor, and mapping decision. For example if a group is unknown it gets flagged and sent to an admin queue.
[08:03] Maya Reyes: How are admin approvals handled when someone requests elevated privileges?
[08:07] Priya Patel: We have a built-in approval workflow that integrates with Jira/ServiceNow. A role elevation request creates a ticket, and RBAC change isn't applied until approved. We record approver info in audit logs.
[08:19] Daniel Kim: For encryption keys, is Redwood accessing our CMK directly or via IAM role?
[08:25] Priya Patel: We never hold key material. The runtime uses IAM roles to call KMS in your account; the CMK policies grant the runtime principal encrypt/decrypt permissions. Redwood code will not export plaintext keys.
[08:34] Maya Reyes: Good. About data residency: if we need EU-only storage, can logs/artifacts be constrained to a region?
[08:41] Priya Patel: Yes, for Private we deploy in your region or allow you to pick region constraints. Artifacts and logs can be stored in your region-specific bucket. For Hosted we have region options but Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[08:54] Sara O'Neill: A few gotchas we've seen with other vendors: late deprovisioning windows, role mapping drift, and missing audit context. Do you have mitigations?
[09:04] Priya Patel: We mitigate with near-real-time SCIM delta sync, periodic reconciliation jobs, and we version role mappings in config repo so you can review diffs. Audit context includes request traces and original IdP assertion.
[09:18] Maya Reyes: Can we run a quick proof-of-concept for SSO + SCIM and a sample RBAC template? We want to verify deprovisioning and scoped deploys.
[09:26] Alex Chen: Absolutely — that's our usual pilot. We'll stand up a sandbox Private control plane in your VPC and run through Okta integration and a few test users. Priya will assist with mapping.
[09:35] Daniel Kim: Timeline: we'd like pilot next week if possible.
[09:38] Alex Chen: Sounds doable. We'll confirm availability in follow-up.
[09:42] Priya Patel: I'll add a checklist: pre-reqs (IdP metadata, SCIM base URL, cert type), test accounts, and network rules.
[09:51] Maya Reyes: One more question on SAML attributes: do you support signed assertions and encryption of assertion payloads?
[09:57] Priya Patel: We fully support signed assertions — you can provide IdP certs. Assertion encryption is supported in our Private deployments if you request AES-based encrypted assertions; we decrypt inside the control plane. That requires us to have the SP decrypt key which you can manage in your KMS if you prefer.
[10:16] Sara O'Neill: On logging, can we get per-request telemetry like latency and model used for each inference request in audit?
[10:23] Priya Patel: We include request metadata (model-id, route-id, latency, tokens) in operational logs. For PII/PI data we can strip payloads; the audit log stores metadata and decision context.
[10:34] Daniel Kim: If we need to meet ISO controls for encryption, do you have mapping docs?
[10:39] Priya Patel: Yes, we maintain an ISO 27001 controls mapping and configuration guidance; we'll share that along with SOC 2 report under NDA.
[10:48] Alex Chen: OK let's capture short-term blockers. Maya?
[10:51] Maya Reyes: We need the SSO runbook, SCIM mapping examples, and sample RBAC templates. Also confirmation that logs can be exported to our S3 with object lock enabled.
[10:59] Alex Chen: Noted. Priya?
[11:01] Priya Patel: I'll put together the RBAC templates and ensure the runbook covers mTLS, cert rotation, and SCIM mapping for nested groups.
[11:10] Daniel Kim: We'll share Okta metadata and a small test Okta org for the pilot.
[11:15] Alex Chen: Great. Any other questions?
[11:18] Sara O'Neill: One last quick one — how are emergency access / break-glass scenarios handled?
[11:23] Priya Patel: Break-glass users can be created but require multi-party approval; we keep those accounts in a separate audit stream with stricter retention and alerts. We can also integrate with your vault for temporary creds.
[11:36] Maya Reyes: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[11:38] Alex Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot.
[11:42] [END]
